subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should maintainers invest in a current-main live/source reproduction to identify the redirect-mutation boundary before any fix PR is queued?
rationale: The issue is plausible and user-facing, but the inspected current-main exec and tool-call paths preserve command strings; choosing a fix layer without boundary proof risks repairing the wrong component.

options.title: Reproduce before repair
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main exec/tool-call reproduction that identifies whether the bug is in provider streaming, tool-call repair, gateway authorization rendering, or another bridge.

options.title: Close as needs-info later
options.body: If no current-main proof can be produced after a reasonable maintainer attempt, close with a request for fresh logs or a recording from the latest release.

options.title: Queue speculative coverage
options.body: Add redirect-preservation tests across likely boundaries without changing runtime behavior, but avoid a behavior fix until one of those tests fails.

recommendation.title: Reproduce before repair
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main exec/tool-call reproduction that identifies whether the bug is in provider streaming, tool-call repair, gateway authorization rendering, or another bridge.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent exec runtime history makes this the best available owner for deciding whether to pursue deeper runtime reproduction first.
